- Model consistently overestimates prices in the short term after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is bullish or neutral; apply downward bias correction for 3–5 days post-peak.
- When sentiment is bearish or mixed, model fails to anticipate sharp declines; reduce forecast slope and add early mean-reversion trigger if 3 consecutive days show downward momentum.
- In high-event periods (e.g., auction-heavy weeks), model overreacts to supply news; dampen forecast growth by 10–15% if supply_net is negative and sentiment is neutral or bearish.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag in direction change; adjust forecast to align with sentiment shift 1–2 days ahead.
- For 30-day forecasts, model exhibits persistent upward bias when recent prices are trending down; apply a “mean-reversion floor” at 1–2 standard deviations below recent 10-day average.
- Overshoot after bullish sentiment spikes is common; cap forecast growth at 2–3% per day after peak unless sentiment remains strong.
- When sentiment is consistently negative or neutral, model underestimates downside risk; add 5–10% buffer for early decline if supply_net is negative and sentiment < 0.5.
